claims.text: A predictive model incorporating atomic mass variance, atomic radius mismatch, and chemical disorder can accurately identify high-entropy alloys with low phonon thermal conductivity.
Atomic mass variance, atomic radius mismatch, and chemical disorder induce significant local lattice distortions in high-entropy alloys.
Local lattice distortions enhance phonon scattering.
The intended materials are single-phase, disordered high-entropy alloys, including refractory HEAs with predominantly BCC or FCC structures.
The alloys should be synthesized to maximize chemical disorder and avoid secondary-phase precipitation.
A machine-learning model using relevant alloy descriptors will be applied to screen HEA compositions for low phonon thermal conductivity.
Testing from room temperature to moderate temperatures provides a regime in which lattice dynamics dominate.
Chemical disorder and the resulting local lattice distortions mediate enhanced phonon scattering.
Variations in atomic mass and atomic size create local lattice distortions in HEAs.
The resulting local lattice distortions act as stronger phonon-scattering centers.
Quantitatively including mass variance, size mismatch, and disorder descriptors enables better forecasts of phonon thermal conductivity than models based on average alloy properties.
HEAs selected by the model will have low measured phonon thermal conductivity relative to the expectations of conventional predictive methods.
The proposed approach may improve prediction accuracy by approximately 20% relative to baseline approaches.
Conventional models use average alloy properties and neglect local-disorder effects.
Neglecting local-disorder effects causes significant prediction error for phonon thermal conductivity in HEAs.
The approach is expected to apply only to single-phase, highly disordered HEAs.
Significant secondary phases can make the model unreliable.
At extreme high temperatures, additional anharmonic effects can dominate and make the model unreliable.
Processing-induced microstructural variations may affect prediction performance.
Failure to obtain a statistically significant accuracy improvement over conventional methods, operationalized as less than 5% improvement, would falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The predicted improvement is approximately 20%, but the falsification threshold is only less than 5%; outcomes between 5% and 20% would miss the stated prediction without falsifying the hypothesis.

The mechanism invokes enhanced phonon scattering, but the falsification rule says this scattering can be verified by microstructural characterization, which measures structure rather than phonon-scattering rates directly.
